chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: End of the Goldkette band and the move to New York with Adrian Rollini
summary: Morehouse thought Rollini's New Yorkers one of the finest groups; Virginia tells of Whiteman wooing the Goldkette men and the last Roseland booking, after which Rollini took Chauncey to New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Adrian Rollini. No, he wasn't with Adrian Rollini.
No.
That's what I wanted to ask you about next. After the Goldkett band broke up, they went bankrupt I guess. They lost all their money anyway.
Yeah.
And some of the members went with Adrian Rollini, New Yorkers. Remember them?
Yeah.

You once had some very fine words to say about that band. Do you remember what they were? You had very high regard for that group. Do you remember what that group was like that you thought so much of them for? Adrian Rollini.
No, I don't remember.
You once told somebody, some interviewer years ago, that you thought that was one of the finest bands, one of the finest groups you'd ever played with.
Yeah.
Because they all admired each other so much.
That's right.
And they didn't have any jealousy toward each other. Do you remember that?
Do you have any record of when the Goldkett band played Atlantic City just before their last
engagement at the Roseland Ballroom?
I'm aware that they played Atlantic City. I don't know anything about it now.
Paul Whiteman was playing there at the time.
No, I didn't know that.
And he was wooing these boys away.
He dropped by to listen. I mean he'd listen. He didn't drop by. He was there. He listened to the Goldkett band.
He listened, yeah.
He listened to them. And he wanted all of them.
Oh really. He wanted everything.

He wanted all of them. They had this one more booking that Korko Keith had for them in New York. They were trying to hold together very very much so. But this was the last engagement that Keith was able to get for them. /Korko? Korko?
The Atlantic City one.
No, no.
Which one?
The one more at Roseland Ballroom.
Oh Roseland, of course, right.
And that's where they really disbanded.
That was 1928, was that?
I don't know the year. The records would show that.
Yes, of course.
Then Chauncey had a choice of going with Whiteman or...he wanted to...most of the boys went with Whiteman.
First it was Adrian Rollini though.
Yes.
Yeah.
Adrian Rollini told Chauncey, let's go to New York.
Uh huh.
That's how that - they became, you and Adrian Rollini got together somehow.
Yeah. That's why I got Adrian Rollini here.
I don't remember the exact facts there but from that grew his contracts with radio and television.
